title: The Solution to the Dicee Challenge
section: 17. Boss Level Challenge 1 - The Dicee Game
summary: Step-by-step walkthrough of the Dicee solution: link an external script, set default dice images, generate two random 1-6 numbers, build image paths with string concatenation, update both img elements with setAttribute, and announce the winner in the h1 with an if / else if / else chain. Ends with advice on balancing short and readable code.

concepts.heading: Step 1: external script
points: Create a JS file (index.js) in the project and link it with a script tag whose src is that file.
Place the tag just before the closing body tag, the same position used for other external resources in earlier modules.
Quick test: put an alert in the file, reload, and see the alert to confirm the link works. Remove it afterwards.

concepts.heading: Step 2: default images
points: Both img src values start as images/dice6.png. Dice files live in an images folder and are named dice1 to dice6, so the folder must be part of the path.
The src must include the folder name (plural 'images') followed by a slash.

concepts.heading: Step 3: random number recap
points: Math.random() gives a decimal from 0 up to just under 1.
Multiplying by 6 widens it to 0 up to just under 6.
Math.floor drops the decimals, leaving integers 0-5.
Adding 1 shifts the range to 1-6.
Any piece of code can be pasted into the console to inspect its output, which helps verify each step.
If this is unclear, revisit the earlier randomisation lesson.

concepts.heading: Step 4: building the image path
points: Because file names are dice1.png to dice6.png, string concatenation of 'dice' + number + '.png' picks the right file.
A second variable prepends 'images/'. This split into separate variables is optional and used only to make each step visible; one expression would do.
Select the first image with document.querySelectorAll('img')[0]. querySelectorAll returns a list of all matching elements, so index 0 is the first (left) image and index 1 is the second.
Call setAttribute('src', randomImageSource) on it: first argument is the attribute name, second is the new value.
After reloading, the left die shows a random face each time.

concepts.heading: Step 5: second image
points: Repeat with a second variable randomNumber2 using the same formula, a second source string, and querySelectorAll('img')[1].
Recommendation: type the repeated code out instead of copy-pasting, because pasted duplicates tend to leave stale variable names that cause bugs.
The second version condenses lines to show that the variable and select/set steps can be merged.

concepts.heading: Step 6: announcing the winner
points: Use an if / else if / else: first branch randomNumber1 greater than randomNumber2 means Player 1 wins; else if randomNumber2 is greater means Player 2 wins; the final else covers equal values, a draw.
Each branch sets innerHTML of document.querySelector('h1'). querySelector is enough because the page has one h1.
Emoji can be added to the message text: on Mac via Edit > Emoji & Symbols, on Windows by searching for the emoji in the browser.

concepts.heading: Alternatives and code readability
points: Other valid approaches: getElementById, getElementsByTagName/ClassName, or querySelector with classes (the starter gives the images classes) instead of querySelectorAll indexes.
The code can be refactored shorter, but compress with care. Very short code that crams many operations into one line is hard to read.
Aim for a balance between concise and expressive. The walkthrough version is deliberately somewhat long to be clear.
(Extra) Prefer let/const over var in modern code, and a function for the repeated roll logic.
Next module covers responding to events such as clicks and key presses.

task.name: Dicee game
task.starting_point: Skeleton project: index.html with h1 'Refresh Me', two img elements, styles.css, images folder (dice1-6).
task.goal: On each refresh show two random dice faces and a headline naming the winner or a draw.
steps: Create index.js and link it before </body>; test with an alert.
Set both img src values to images/dice6.png.
Build the image path with concatenation and set the first img src via setAttribute.
Repeat for randomNumber2 and the second img.
Compare the numbers with if / else if / else and set the h1 innerHTML.
task.expected_result: Refresh gives two random dice and a matching result message.
task.reference_repo_path: Section 17 - Boss Level Challenge 1 - The Dicee Game

pitfalls: Forgetting + 1 so dice 0 is requested (broken image).
Using querySelector (single) for the images and getting only the first one, or off-by-one indexes with querySelectorAll.
Copy-pasting code and leaving randomNumber1 in the second block.
Missing 'images/' folder prefix in the src.
Reference repo differs slightly: it uses class selectors .img1 / .img2, ./images/ paths, === first for draw, and adds flag emoji and a personal footer (ignore the footer).
